title: Adaptive surge-quarantine autoscaler: composite targets + safety fences
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: current autoscalers either react to single metrics (e.g., p95 latency or per-GPU throughput) or allow large step ups that create noisy falls in QoS and cost spikes. We need an autoscaling policy engine tailored for Dedicated fleets that: 1) expresses composite target metrics (latency percentiles + normalized token throughput + queue depth + error rate), 2) runs a hybrid scaling algorithm that balances responsiveness and stability, and 3) enforces hard safety limits and quarantine behavior during anomalous events.
background: Dedicated customers require throughput guarantees and predictable unit costs. Existing work (see ENG-4127, ENG-15432) sets guardrails but doesn't cover anomaly quarantine or composite target fusion. This ticket defines and implements a new policy primitive 'quarantine-surge' which gates aggressive scale-ups when signals indicate unhealthy or non-user-driven load (e.g., traffic storms, retries, or misbehaving tenants).
acceptance_criteria:
- Implement composite metric definition API: allow policies to reference p50/p95/p99 latency, per-GPU token throughput, request queue depth, request error rate (5xx), and a derived 'traffic-stability' score.
- Implement hybrid algorithm: proportional-integral controller + capped additive surge credits + decay-based headroom accounting.
- Add quarantine mode: when anomaly detectors flag instability (spike in errors or extreme variance), scale-ups are limited to a controlled quarantine band and non-essential burst credits are revoked.
- Safety limits enforced: max scale-up rate (x% of current fleet per minute), max total replicas per tenant, min stable replica floor, and rollback window if downstream metrics worsen post-scale.
- Unit tests, integration tests with simulator, and a canary rollout to 2 non-production fleets.
- Dashboard surfaces policy decisions and historical quaratine events.
- Documentation and runbook for ops + feature flag to disable new behavior.
implementation_plan: 1) Policy DSL: add 'composite_target' stanza to policy language (schema docs updated). 2) Metric fusion: implement a small service that computes the fused target value from multiple time series (p99 -> weight, throughput normalized by instance capacity, queue depth normalized). 3) Controller: implement PI loop with surge-credit bank that can be debited for one-step additive increases. 4) Quarantine detector: reuse error-rate and variance detectors from ENG-4127; add hysteresis and muting of credits. 5) Safety enforcement: global rate limiter in orchestrator to cap replica adds/removals. 6) Telemetry: emit decision events and reasons (scale_decision:{reason, delta, pre_metrics, post_metrics}). 7) Tests & sim: expand autoscaler simulator with synthetic anomalies to validate quarantine behavior. 8) Canary rollout: feature-flagged deploy to staging fleets, gradual ramp to low-traffic dedicated fleets, evaluate 48h metrics, then broader rollout.
telemetry_and_metrics: New metrics to emit: autoscaler.composite_target_value, autoscaler.surge_credits, autoscaler.quarantine_state{on|off}, autoscaler.scale_decision_reason, autoscaler.max_rate_violation. Existing metrics to be consumed: runtime.p95_latency, runtime.p99_latency, runtime.tokens_per_gpu, runtime.queue_depth, runtime.error_5xx_rate. Dashboards: per-tenant policy decisions, quarantine incidents, cost delta vs baseline.
sim_results_summary: Local simulator runs (1000 synthetic traces) show: - Without quarantine: 12% of traces produced oscillations >3 scale cycles resulting in 18% higher cost. - With quarantine + surge-credit bank: oscillations reduced to 1.8% and median latency improved by 9ms under bursty loads; tail behavior improved on noisy traces. Detailed sim artifacts uploaded to drive link below.

risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: false positives in quarantine could throttle legitimate user growth -> mitigation: conservative default thresholds, 2-stage hysteresis, and a 'manual-override' feature flag for customer success.
Risk: telemetry volume increase -> mitigation: sample decision events in high-cardinality tenants, compress aggregated events for long-term storage.
Risk: complexity in policy DSL -> mitigation: provide presets (latency-first, throughput-first, cost-conservative) and UI templates in Console.
rollout_and_monitoring: Rollout steps: 1) staging fleets (immediate), 2) 2 low-traffic Dedicated tenants (48h observation), 3) 10% of small/medium fleets, 4) ramp to wider population. Alerting: create SLO guard alerts for p95/p99 regressions, cost-per-token anomalies, and repeated scale oscillation detection. Runbook: rollback to previous autoscaler policy, revoke surge credits, and open incident for debug.
notes: This ticket intentionally avoids changing the user-facing API now; changes are behind a feature flag to allow iterative tuning. Coordinate with Customer Success before enabling on any paid Dedicated tenants. Consider a beta program for high-volume customers that want aggressive surge behavior.
